editorial:
Imagine you are living in old Ireland, where the weather is gray and a scary crop disease is about to ruin everything. You meet Colmán, a hardworking fisherman who just wants to keep his family safe. When a local priest asks him to let a stranger named Patsy stay at his house, Colmán agrees, even though he is unsure about it. Patsy is a former soldier with a rough past, and his arrival brings a lot of tension into the home. You will feel the stress growing as these two very different men try to get along while the world around them falls apart.

The acting is the best part here because the tension between the lead actors feels real. It is a slow burn, meaning it takes its time to build up the drama, which might be too slow for some, but it makes the payoff better. If you enjoy stories about survival and human nature, you will love this. Since the scenery is so beautiful and gritty, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best look. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this one.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the hidden tensions between Colmán and Patsy explode into violence. You find out that Patsy was not just a random soldier, but carried heavy guilt and secrets from his past. After a final, brutal struggle, the movie ends with a sad realization about how fear and desperation can turn good people into monsters. It wraps up by showing that the blight destroyed more than just the food; it destroyed their souls too.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and psychological thrillers.
